strings.两人被拉开，一个往北，一个往南。第二天中午，他们在大椰子树下碰了面，谁也没提昨天: They were pulled apart, one north, one south. At noon the next day they met under the big coconut palm, and neither mentioned yesterday.

strings.两天过去了。海面上什么也没有——没有船，没有飞机。有人开始小声说：晃翅膀也许只是: Two days pass. There is nothing on the sea — no boat, no plane. People start to say it quietly: maybe rocking the wings was just the pilot waving; maybe he never saw people at all, only an island.

strings.举着火把下去求救: Go down with torches and ask for rescue.

strings.事故报告里写着：船长值班时饮酒，在舵位上睡着。韩振海被判了两年，缓刑三年。后来他: The accident report said: the captain drank on watch and fell asleep at the helm. Neil Han was given two years, suspended for three. strings.兰多埋在了 Jun-Jun 旁边。两座坟，两个浮木十字架，一个刻着 JUN-JU: Lando is buried beside Joey. Two graves, two driftwood crosses, one carved JUN-JUN and one carved LANDO, cut with the point of his own harpoon.
strings.兰多找到了 payao 的位置，可那里只剩下几根断了的竹竿——今年的风浪把它打散: Lando found the payao's position, but only a few broken bamboo poles were left — this year's wind and waves had scattered it and the mother boat had stopped coming. He dragged the bangka up the beach and did not speak all day.
strings.兰多把自己的蓝塑料桶拖出了窝棚，又把鱼叉、那半袋晒干的鱼都背上了肩。他指了指南头: Lando drags his blue plastic barrel out of the shack and shoulders his spear and his half-sack of dried fish. strings.原型：1965 年，六个汤加少年偷了一条渔船出海，漂到无人岛 'Ata。他们约定: Where it comes from: in 1965 six Tongan boys stole a fishing boat and put to sea, and drifted to the uninhabited island of 'Ata. They agreed to work in pairs on shifts, kept a fire burning day and night, and when they quarrelled they split up to opposite ends of the island to cool off and made it up the next day; on coconuts, seabirds, fish and rainwater caught in hollowed tree trunks they lasted fifteen months, and every one of them lived — a true ending that is the exact opposite of Lord of the Flies. In 1629 the Dutch East India Company's Batavia struck a reef off the west coast of Australia; after the captain took a boat for help, the under-merchant Cornelis talked a following round on the island, took control of the water and the food, and massacred more than a hundred survivors on the grounds that fewer mouths meant a better chance of living; the soldiers under Hayes, driven off to another small island to die, found water there instead and in the end beat the mutineers. In 1761 the French ship Utile ran aground on Tromelin in the Indian Ocean; her crew built a boat from the wreck and sailed away, leaving eighty Malagasy slaves on an island of less than one square kilometre with no trees. They dug wells for brackish groundwater and held on for fifteen years on seabirds, sea turtles and a fire they never let go out; when rescue finally came, only seven women and an eight-month-old baby were left. The shift fire watch, the wells of brackish water, the hollowed trunks for rainwater, the booby catching and the factions fighting over water and food in this scenario are all drawn from these three true stories.

strings.在岛中间的灌木丛里挖个深坑当茅坑，用完拿沙子盖上: Dig a deep pit in the scrub in the middle of the island and cover it with sand after use
strings.在沙滩上烧一大堆火: Build a big fire on the beach
strings.在沙滩上用白珊瑚石摆出巨大的 SOS，爬上北头的岩石高地瞭望；空下来就往高地上背: Lay out a huge SOS on the beach in white coral stone and climb the rock high ground at the north end to keep watch; in any spare hour, carry firewood up there and pile the signal fire.
strings.在海上漂流的人就是这么撑下来的；鸟群会被吓走一截: That's how castaways adrift at sea have survived; it'll scare off a chunk of the colony
strings.在礁盘外缘海葬: Burial at sea past the edge of the reef flat
strings.在离海远一点的沙地上挖坑，等地下水慢慢渗出来。来得快、量也大，但水是咸的：混进存: Dig a pit in the sand further back from the sea and let the groundwater seep in. It comes fast and in quantity, but the water is salty: mixed into your stores it gives you diarrhoea and leaves you thirstier. Rain dilutes it.
strings.地产老板的独子，他父亲是训练营最大的赞助商。会说话、会来事，出手大方，上船第一天: Only son of a property developer, his father the camp's biggest sponsor. Good with words, good with people, free with his money: the first day aboard he treated everyone to a seafood dinner. When they abandoned ship, he was the first one onto the liferaft.
strings.坐下来谈：水桶搬回原处，但账由陆子昂来管: Sit down and talk: the drums go back where they were, but Ryan Lu keeps the tally.
strings.坑底慢慢渗出一层水，用椰子壳一点一点地刮。水有一点涩，但喝得下去。: A film of water slowly seeps into the bottom of each pit, scraped up a coconut shell at a time. It's a little brackish, but drinkable.
strings.坑挖得很浅。那天晚上，没有人愿意往那个方向看。: The hole was shallow. That night nobody would look that way.
strings.多一张嘴、多一个伤员，也多一个会潜水的年轻人: One more mouth, one more wounded man — and one more young diver.
strings.多一张嘴，也多一个在这座岛上活了三个月的人: One more mouth — and one more who has lived three months on this island
strings.多劳多得：干活的人先吃饱，不干活的少分: More work, more reward: those who work eat first, those who do not get less
strings.多存一些，也给以后留下容器；救生筏留着，以后能绑在木筏底下当浮筒: Stores more, and leaves containers for later; the liferaft is kept to lash under the raft as a float later
strings.夜里去北头抓鲣鸟：喝血，吃肉: Go to the north end at night for boobies: drink the blood, eat the meat
strings.夜里没人守着，火堆一点点暗下去，天亮时只剩一堆冷灰。: No one kept the fire watch; the fire dimmed by degrees, and by first light there was nothing left but cold ash.
strings.夜里的礁盘有暗流，也有石头鱼: The night reef has currents, and stonefish
strings.够所有人饱饱地吃一顿；也可能所有人一起中毒: Enough for everyone to eat their fill; or everyone poisoned together
strings.大声喊他往回走: Shout at him to turn back
strings.大声喊：“快来看！锚仔刨出来一个包！”: Shout: "Come and look! Anchor has dug out a bag!"
strings.大家只抓了十来只，又从草窝里摸了些蛋。鸟群骚动了一阵，又安静了下来。: They took only a dozen or so and gathered a few eggs from the grass nests. The flock stirred, then settled again.
strings.大家在北头礁岩背阴的一面插上木棍，铺了厚厚一层椰叶。晓雨被抬了进去，小声说了好几: Poles were driven into the shaded face of the reef rock at the north end and a thick layer of palm fronds laid over them. Ivy was carried in and whispered her thanks again and again.
strings.大家在高地上搭了个小小的遮阳棚，排好了瞭望的班。小石头抢着要值第一班。: They put up a small sunshade on the high ground and drew up a rota for the watch. Pebble insisted on taking the first shift.
strings.大家把能找到的每一个椰子壳、罐头盒都排在了窝棚边上，又用帆布多拉了一道槽。: They lined up every coconut shell and tin can they could find along the side of the shack, and ran another trough out of canvas.
strings.大家用椰叶给他搭了个小棚，轮流守着，按时给他翻身。: They build him a little palm-frond shelter and take turns sitting with him, turning him on schedule.
strings.大家盯着那块纱布，谁也不敢碰。: Everyone stares at the gauze; nobody dares touch it.
strings.大家看着那条船在天边兜完最后一圈，消失了。: They watch the ship complete its last circle on the horizon and vanish.
strings.大家还能不能坐在一堆火边吃饭。偷水、偷懒、配给不公、拉帮结派、动手打人都会让人心: Whether everyone can still sit down and eat at one fire. Stealing water, slacking off, unfair rations, cliques and thrown punches all pull morale apart.
strings.大家饿着肚子，看着满树的鸟。老渔民都知道：跟着鸟群走，就能找到鱼群；有鱼群的地方: They watched the tree full of birds on empty stomachs. Every old fisherman knows it: follow the birds and you find the fish; where the fish are, the boats come.
strings.大晴天几乎一定能成: On a clear day it will almost certainly work.
strings.大鱼被扔回了海里。有人在旁边狠狠地咽了一口口水。: The big fish went back into the sea. Someone nearby swallowed hard.
strings.大鱼，no。巴掌大的，可以吃。大的，毒。: Big fish, no. Palm-sized, can eat. Big ones, poison.
strings.天一擦黑，高地上就亮起了一团火。守火的人轮着班，谁也不让它小下去。: As soon as dusk falls, a fire blazes on the high ground. The watch takes turns and nobody lets it die down.
strings.天亮了。“海燕号”斜卡在礁盘外缘，断桅泡在水里，船身每挨一个浪就往下沉一点。八个: Morning came. The Petrel lay jammed at an angle on the outer edge of the reef flat, her broken mast soaking in the water, the hull settling a little lower with every wave. Eight people and a dog were crowded on to the scalding sand with only a half-full drum of fresh water at hand. The sun had barely risen and the skin already stung. What first?
strings.天亮的时候，两拨人隔着那片椰林，谁也不看谁。沙地上的血迹被潮水冲了一整天才冲干净: By dawn the two groups kept to either side of the palm grove and would not look at each other. The tide took a whole day to wash the blood out of the sand.
strings.天亮的时候，兰多的铺位空了。他带走了他的鱼叉和那只蓝桶，回到了南头的棚子里——像: By morning Lando's bed was empty. He had taken his harpoon and the blue drum and gone back to his shelter at the south end — living alone, the way he had before you came.
strings.天太热，存着的鱼、贝和鸟肉一夜之间又臭了一截（{var.spoil}）。苍蝇围着: In this heat, another heap of stored fish, shellfish and bird meat has gone off overnight ({var.spoil}). Flies drone round the shack.
strings.天快亮了。船老大蹲在沙滩上抽烟，说只能捎一个人，送到北部湾随便哪个渔港的码头：“: It was almost light. The boat boss crouched on the sand, smoking, and said he could take one person, no more, and set them down at any fishing port in the Gulf of Tonkin: "Once you're ashore, have your family wire the money. Whether you go to the police is your business — only never say you saw us."
strings.天快亮时，两个人拎着一串鱼、两只乌贼回来了。兰多看见礁盘边上的符秀英，愣了一下，: Near dawn the two come back with a string of fish and two squid. Lando sees Susan Fu at the reef's edge, hesitates, and holds out the biggest fish.
strings.天快亮时，海龟慢慢爬回了海里。大家刨开沙坑，捧出来一个个乒乓球大小的软壳蛋。: Towards dawn the turtle crawled slowly back to the sea. They dug open the nest and lifted out soft-shelled eggs, each the size of a table-tennis ball.
strings.天还没亮，{actor} 看见陆子昂一个人往北头的礁岩走，在一道石缝前蹲了很久。: Before dawn {actor} saw Ryan Lu walking alone towards the reef rock at the north end and crouching a long time at a crack in the stone. When he came back there was a crumb of biscuit at the corner of his mouth.
strings.天黑以后，北头的抗风桐上落满了红脚鲣鸟。它们从没见过人，伸手就能从树枝上抓下来；: After dark the pisonia at the north end was crowded with red-footed boobies. They had never seen a human; you could reach out and take them off the branches. In the grass nests below there were clutch after clutch of eggs.
strings.天黑以后，海面上再也找不到那个人影了。: After dark there's no sign of {actor.him} anywhere on the water.
strings.天黑前，沙滩上的 SOS 每个字母都有十几步长，旁边一支白色的箭头直指礁盘的缺口: By dark, each letter of the SOS on the beach is a dozen paces long, and a white arrow beside it points straight at the gap in the reef.
strings.太远了，追不上。好在外面的人又开始找这一带了: Too far; there's no catching them. At least they're searching this area again
strings.太阳毒得像火，白沙晃得睁不开眼，礁盘上的积水被晒得发烫。: The sun burns like fire, the white sand is blinding, and the pools on the reef flat are hot underfoot.
strings.太阳这么毒，晒一晒什么都死了，不用大惊小怪: In this sun everything dries up and dies anyway. No need to fuss
strings.她也许能扛过去，也许不能: She might pull through. She might not.
strings.她会把伤口割开一点: She will open the wound a little
strings.她的份减半，省下的给干重活的人: Halve her portion and give the rest to those doing the heavy work
strings.她能最先见到医生；可她说得清这座岛在哪儿吗？: She'd see a doctor first; but could she say clearly where this island is?
strings.她补了二十年网，绑浮杆的手艺不会差: She's mended nets for twenty years; lashing outriggers won't be beyond her
strings.好动、胆大、嘴馋，最怕妈妈哭。: Restless, bold, always hungry; what he fears most is his mother crying.
strings.嫩椰子一个接一个砍开，清甜的椰子水顺着{protagonist}干裂的嘴角流进去: Young coconuts are hacked open one after another, and the sweet water trickles in past {protagonist}'s cracked lips.
strings.嫩椰子水有糖有钾，二战时太平洋上的医生拿它救过人；够得着的椰子会少一截: Young coconut water has sugar and potassium — doctors in the Pacific saved lives with it in the Second World War; the reachable coconuts will go down
strings.存水多，人还得渴一会儿: More water stored; everyone stays thirsty a while longer
strings.存水见底的时候，天终于阴了下来。中午，第一滴雨砸在滚烫的礁岩上，紧接着，一道灰色: When the stored water was nearly gone, the sky finally clouded over. At noon the first drop struck the hot reef rock, and then a grey curtain of rain came pushing in off the sea.
strings.学校帆船社的，第一次出远海。弃船时被浪拍在礁盘上，右小腿被珊瑚划开一道很深的口子: In her school sailing club, and her first time on the open sea. When they abandoned ship a wave slammed her onto the reef flat and coral opened a deep gash in her right calf; she still cannot walk.
strings.孩子会觉得丢脸，兰多会觉得被冤枉: The boy will be humiliated; Lando will feel wronged
strings.孩子先走；可一个十二岁的孩子，要怎么跟警察说清楚这座岛？: The child goes first; but how does a twelve-year-old explain this island to the police?
strings.孩子嘴里的话，大人有时候听得进去: Adults sometimes listen to what a child says
strings.孩子坐得住吗？: Can a boy sit still for it?
strings.孩子水性好，也许自己能回来: The boy swims well; maybe he can get back on his own
strings.孩子需要一点盼头: The boy needs something to look forward to
strings.守住誓言：活着回去，而且不对任何人动手: Keep the oath: go home alive, and never lay a hand on anyone
strings.守夜的人一刻钟叫醒一次自己，扶起{protagonist}的头喂一口。天亮时，{: The night watch wakes every quarter hour to lift {protagonist}'s head for a mouthful. At dawn {protagonist} passes a little urine, and everyone breathes again.
strings.定死规矩：只在南头退潮线以下解手，潮水会冲走；水桶加盖，狗不许靠近水，饭前用海水: Lay down a hard rule: only below the low-tide line at the south end, where the tide washes it away; lids on the water, the dog kept off it, hands scrubbed with seawater before eating
strings.寄居蟹都能吃，人应该也能吃吧: If hermit crabs can eat them, a person should be able to
strings.对不起……又要麻烦你们给我换药。: Sorry... I have to trouble you to change my dressing again.
strings.小石头从石缝里拖出一个橙色的防水包，举过头顶，大声喊他妈妈过来看。: Pebble dragged the orange waterproof bag out of the crack, held it over his head and shouted for his mother to come and see.
strings.小石头听见了，扔下章鱼，连滚带爬地跑了回来。: Pebble heard, dropped the octopus and scrambled back.
strings.小石头埋在北头的高地上，坟边插着他叉章鱼用的那根木叉。后来潭门的渔民听说了这件事: Pebble is buried on the high ground at the north end, the wooden spear he used for octopus planted at the graveside. When the Tanmen fishermen heard, they began throwing a handful of sweets into the sea every time they passed the reef flat.
strings.小石头学会了三个和弦，从早弹到晚，弹得所有人耳朵起茧。没人让他停。: Pebble learned three chords and played from morning to night until everyone's ears were sore. No one told him to stop.
strings.小石头把手表戴在细细的手腕上，表带扣到了最里面一格，还是松的。他在礁岩上刻下了第: Pebble straps the watch round his thin wrist; even on the last hole it's loose. He scratches the first number into the rock.
strings.小石头拉着兰多的手，一路走到椰林边上，又一路拉了回来。符秀英站在窝棚口，没有拦。: Pebble takes Lando's hand and walks him all the way to the edge of the palms — and then all the way back. Susan Fu stands at the mouth of the shack and doesn't stop him.
strings.小石头留在了那座岛上。符秀英回到文昌以后，每年开海那天都会搭潭门的渔船出去一趟，: Pebble stayed on that island. After Susan Fu returned to Wenchang, every year on the day the season opened she would take a Tanmen fishing boat out, scatter a handful of rice beyond the reef flat and set a coconut adrift. The skippers all know her, and never take her money.
strings.小石头被推上了小艇，一直回头喊他妈妈。: Pebble was pushed into the dinghy, calling back for his mother the whole way.
strings.小石头被那条黑船放在北海的一个渔港码头上，在派出所里坐了一夜，才有人相信他说的话: The black ship put Pebble ashore on a fishing-harbour dock in Beihai; he sat in the police station all night before anyone believed what he said. Afterwards he always said it was the longest night of his life, longer than any night on the island.
strings.小石头长大以后考了潜水教练证，在三亚带游客看珊瑚。他左手腕上文着一串数字，是那座: When he grew up, Pebble earned his dive instructor's certificate and takes tourists to see coral in Sanya. On his left wrist is a tattoo of a string of numbers: the coordinates of that unnamed island. When tourists ask, he says: "I spent a summer there."
strings.小艇上还守着一个人。黑暗里一阵扭打，{actor} 捂着淌血的胳膊逃了回来。天亮: Someone was still guarding the dinghy. There was a scuffle in the dark, and {actor} escaped back with a hand pressed to a bleeding arm. Before dawn the black ship weighed anchor and left.
strings.小艇冲上礁盘，伤得最重的人第一批被抬了上去。剩下的人站在齐腰深的水里，一直挥手，: The boat came in over the reef flat and the worst hurt were carried aboard first. The rest stood waist-deep in the water, waving, until the boat turned and came back.
strings.少一口吃的，换一个清静: One mouthful less, and some peace and quiet
strings.就近在沙滩上埋了: Bury it on the beach, close by
strings.山东口音，说话像喊口令：“都听我的！”“慌什么！”“海上的规矩就是规矩。”: A Shandong accent, and he talks like he is barking drill commands: "All of you, do as I say!", "What's the panic?", "Rules at sea are rules."
strings.岛上不能有私产；他会记住这一笔: No private property on this island; he will remember this
strings.岛上的事，留在岛上: What happened on the island stays on the island
strings.岛呈细长的柳叶形，西岸是沙滩，东岸是被浪冲刷的礁岩。窝棚搭在北头岩石高地背风的一: The island is a long, narrow willow leaf: sand on the west shore, wave-scoured reef rock on the east. The shack stands on the leeward side of the rock high ground at the north end, close to both the palm grove and the reef flat.
strings.岛长不到一公里，最宽处三百来米：一圈白沙滩，四十多棵椰子树，岛中间是密密的灌木和: The island is less than a kilometre long and about three hundred metres across at its widest: a ring of white sand, forty-odd coconut palms, dense scrub and pisonia through the middle, and at the north end a rock high ground some ten metres high with seabirds thick in the trees. At low tide the reef flat reaches hundreds of metres out. There is no stream, no spring, not a drop of fresh water.
strings.岸上的人抱着一截椰子树干游了出去，把{actor}拖了回来。: Someone swims out pushing a palm log and tows {actor} back in.
strings.帆船训练营主教练，“海燕号”船长: Head coach of the sailing school, captain of the Petrel
strings.带上船刀和木棍，守在棚子边，等主人回来: Take a boat knife and a club, wait by the shelter for the owner to come back
strings.帮不了他的病，可他会好受一些: It won't help the illness, but he'll feel better
strings.干净水先紧着{actor.ta}：一刻钟一口，一夜不停: Clean water to {actor.him} first: a mouthful every quarter hour, all night
strings.广州一所医学院临床医学专业五年级，暑假报了训练营。上岸后她用救生筏的急救包给晓雨: Fifth-year clinical medicine at a medical school in Guangzhou; she signed up for the camp for the summer. Once ashore she used the liferaft's first-aid kit to stop Ivy's bleeding, and from then on everyone called her Doctor Su.
strings.广州口音的普通话，慢条斯理，说起天气就像在念预报稿：“偏南风三到四级，午后有阵雨: Cantonese-accented Mandarin, unhurried; he speaks of weather as if reading a bulletin: "Southerly winds, force three to four; showers in the afternoon." He calls Pebble "little one".
strings.开海后的第三个礼拜。一个清早，一条从潭门来的木壳渔船在外礁下了锚，船老大带着两个: The third week after the season opening. Early one morning a wooden-hulled fishing boat from Tanmen dropped anchor at the outer reef, and the skipper came ashore in a dinghy with two young men — they had come to gather sea cucumbers and never expected to find anyone on the island.
strings.开海后的第三个礼拜，来捡海参的潭门渔民在这座无名小岛上发现了他们。活着上船的是：: In the third week after the season opened, Tanmen fishermen gathering sea cucumber found them on the unnamed island. Those who lived to board: {survivors}. Those who did not live to see the day: {dead}. Back in port the fishermen said the first thing the islanders asked was not "Where are you from?" but "What's the date?"
strings.弃船时你抢走了船上唯一的防水应急包，偷偷藏在岛北头的礁岩缝里：里面有压缩饼干、两: When the ship was abandoned you took the only waterproof emergency kit aboard and hid it in a crack in the reef rock at the north end: hardtack, two bottles of water, two handheld red flares. You never told anyone.
strings.弓钻在所有人手里传了一圈又一圈。: The bow drill passed from hand to hand, round after round.
strings.当众拿出来，问韩振海那晚到底怎么回事: Bring it out in front of everyone and ask Neil Han what really happened that night
strings.当众揭穿，带大家去礁岩缝里搜: Expose him in front of everyone and search the crack in the rock
strings.当过八年兵，退伍后在深圳做安保主管，攒了两年钱来学帆船。话很少，干活顶两个人；会: Eight years in the army, then head of security in Shenzhen; he saved for two years to learn sailing. He says very little and works like two men; he swims and dives, and always carries a dive knife on his belt. The night they hit the reef, he was the one who dragged Ivy out of the surf.
strings.很费力气，但大家心里会好受一些: Hard work, but everyone will feel a little better.
strings.快刀斩乱麻，代价是有人会记恨: A quick cut through the tangle — but someone will hold a grudge.
strings.憋了这么多天，人能缓过来；要是船不来，喝掉的水就找不回来了: After all these days people will get their strength back; if the boat doesn't come, the water drunk tonight won't come back
strings.成为这座岛上说了算的人：当领头人至少 12 天，并且活着离开: Become the one who decides on this island: lead for at least 12 days, and leave alive
strings.我不疼，真的。你们去睡吧。: It doesn't hurt, really. Go to sleep.
strings.我不饿，真的。给晓雨姐姐吃吧。: I'm not hungry, really. Give it to Ivy.
strings.我可以编椰叶，帽子、席子都行，我的手又没事。: I can weave palm leaves — hats, mats, anything. My hands are fine.
strings.我妈不知道我来航海，我跟她说是去参加夏令营。: My mum doesn't know I came sailing. I told her it was a summer camp.
strings.我妈以为我在北海的冻品厂上班。: My mother thinks I work at a frozen-food plant in Beihai.
strings.我报了三十五年台风，从来没站在它底下过。: I forecast typhoons for thirty-five years and never once stood under one.
strings.我梦见爸爸的船了，他说他来接我们。: I dreamed about Dad's boat. He said he was coming to get us.
strings.我走。上了岸，我家马上派船来: I'll go. Once I'm ashore, my family will send a boat at once.
strings.所有人一起去把水抢回来: Everyone goes together to take the water back
strings.所有人一起往窝棚顶上压椰叶和石头，在礁岩最深的石缝里垒了一道矮墙。有人说：“梁伯: Everyone heaves palm fronds and stones onto the roof and builds a low wall in the deepest cleft. Someone says: “Uncle Leo called it.”
strings.所有人一起往窝棚顶上压椰叶和石头，在礁岩最深的石缝里垒了一道矮墙，把水桶和存粮一: Everyone piled palm fronds and stones onto the shack roof, built a low wall in the deepest crevice of the reef rock and stowed the water drums and the food stores inside, one by one.
strings.所有人一起扯着嗓子喊。: Everyone shouted at the top of their lungs.
strings.所有人互相搀着，踩着礁盘往外走。有人回头看了一眼那个窝棚，说不清是什么心情。: Leaning on one another, they walked out across the reef flat. Someone looked back once at the shack, with a feeling they could not name.
strings.所有人今天都去背柴、搬石头: Everyone spends today carrying firewood and stones
strings.所有人仰着头站在雨里，张大嘴接雨水，喝到肚子发胀。小石头在沙滩上又蹦又跳。: Everyone stood with faces turned up in the rain, mouths wide, drinking until their stomachs were tight. Pebble capered up and down the beach.
strings.所有人仰着头站在雨里，张着嘴，捧着手，喝到肚子发胀。有人笑出了声，笑着笑着就哭了: They stood in the rain with their heads tipped back, mouths open, hands cupped, drinking until their bellies were tight. Someone laughed out loud, and the laughing turned to tears.
strings.所有人冒着雨把桶、椰子壳和帆布槽摆好，看着水一点点涨上来，才轮流凑过去喝几口。: They set out the drums, the coconut shells and the canvas trough in the rain, watched the water creep up, and only then took turns to lean in for a few mouthfuls.
strings.所有人喊着号子，把沉甸甸的木筏一寸一寸地拖上了高地，绑在两块大礁石中间。: Shouting in time, they dragged the heavy raft up to the high ground inch by inch and lashed it between two big rocks.
strings.所有人围在了窝棚口。: Everyone gathers at the mouth of the shack.
strings.所有人拼命往窝棚顶上压椰叶和石头，把水桶和存粮塞进礁岩的石缝。风越来越大。: Everyone fought to pile palm fronds and stones on the shack roof and stuffed the water drums and food stores into crevices in the reef rock. The wind kept rising.
strings.所有人朝北头的礁岩冲了过去。: Everyone charged the reef rock at the north end.
strings.所有人站上高地，用罐头盖、手机屏、刀面对着船反光: Everyone up on the high ground, flashing tin lids, phone screens and the knife blade at the ship
strings.所有人站在雨里，喝到肚子发胀，有人笑着笑着就哭了。: Everyone stands in the rain and drinks until their bellies ache; someone laughs until it turns into crying.
strings.所有人站在雨里，能喝多少喝多少: Everyone stands in the rain and drinks as much as they can hold
strings.所有人趴在灌木丛里，听着礁盘上铁钎撬砗磲的声音响了一整夜。天亮前，铁壳船起锚走了: Everyone lay flat in the scrub and listened to the clam bars working the reef flat all night. Before dawn the iron boat weighed anchor and left, and the reef flat was strewn with prised-open clam shells.
strings.所有人跑上北头的岩石高地，又跳又喊，挥着衣服，直到那个白点消失在天边。: Everyone ran up to the rock ridge at the north end, jumping and shouting and waving their clothes, until the white speck vanished at the horizon.
strings.所有人跑上高地挥衣服，用手机屏幕反光: Everyone run up to the high ground, waving clothes and flashing phone screens
strings.所有人蹲在远处，静静地看着它下完蛋、盖好沙子、一步一步爬回海里。有人说，等回去了: Everyone crouched at a distance and watched it finish laying, cover the sand and crawl, step by step, back to the sea. Someone said that when they got home they would have to tell everyone about this night.
strings.所有人躺在阴凉里，一动不动，熬: Everyone lies still in the shade and endures it
strings.所有人轮流挖了一下午。坟头朝着北边——家的方向。有人念了几句话，声音哑得听不清。: Everyone took turns digging all afternoon. The grave faces north — towards home. Someone said a few words, too hoarse to be made out.
strings.所有人都活着回来了，大家都说是韩船长的功劳。事故报告上写的是“遭遇恶劣天气，偏离: Everyone came back alive, and everyone said it was Captain Han's doing. The accident report read: "heavy weather, a course deviation." He never touched a drink again and never went to sea again; if anyone called him "captain", he did not answer.
strings.所有人都跑了过来。锚仔从石缝里拖出一个橙色的防水应急包，{actor} 第一个蹲: Everyone came running. Anchor dragged an orange waterproof emergency kit out of the crack, and {actor} was the first to crouch down and pull the zip open: the last of the hardtack, water, and two handheld flares. "That dog has done us a huge favour!"
strings.所有能装水的都摆出去，集雨棚绷紧，先存再喝: Put out everything that holds water and pull the catcher tight: store first, drink after
strings.扔回海里，不冒这个险: Throw it back into the sea — do not take the risk
strings.扔进海里，事已至此: Throw it in the sea. What's done is done.
strings.扶他回窝棚，先把伤口洗干净: Help him back to the shack and wash the wound first.
strings.抄起削尖的木棍打回去: Take up a sharpened stick and hit back
strings.把一半的水让给他们，求个太平: Give them half the water and buy some peace
strings.把他抬到高地的遮阳棚里，让他看得见海: Carry him up to the shade on the high ground where he can see the sea
strings.把他的水桶抬回去，当面赔个不是: Carry his drum back and apologise to his face
strings.把所有能装水的东西都摆出去，接台风雨: Put out everything that can hold water and catch the typhoon rain
strings.把抗生素全用在拉得最重的人身上: Give all the antibiotics to the worst cases
strings.把救生筏翻过来当水池，拆下篷布兜雨: Turn the liferaft over for a water tank and rig the canopy to catch the rain
strings.把木筏拖上高地，用缆绳绑死在礁岩上: Drag the raft up to the high ground and lash it down to the reef rock
strings.把棍子扔进海里: Throw the club into the sea
strings.把残帆和椰叶绑在两棵椰子树之间，斜着拉成一个大漏斗，雨水顺着叶脉流进桶里。: Lash the torn sail and palm fronds between two coconut palms, slanted into a big funnel, and the rain runs down the veins of the leaves into the drum.
strings.把海水倒进从船上捞回来的铝锅里烧开，盖上倒扣的锅盖，让蒸汽顺着帆布条滴进椰子壳。: Seawater goes into an aluminium pot salvaged from the ship and is boiled; the lid is set on upside down, and the steam runs down a strip of canvas and drips into a coconut shell. A litre or two a day is all you get, and it burns one and a half loads of firewood, but it is true fresh water.
strings.把海水兑进淡水里喝：一份海水兑两份淡水，水能多撑好几天: Stretch the water with seawater: one part sea to two parts fresh, and it lasts days longer
strings.把火堆烧旺，压上湿椰叶冒浓烟: Stoke the fire and pile on wet palm fronds for thick smoke
strings.把火种护进礁岩深处的石缝: Shelter the embers deep in a crevice in the reef rock
strings.把病人挪到南头的棚子里，别传给别人: Move the sick to the shelter at the south end so it doesn't spread
strings.把药拿出来，告诉大家实话: Bring the medicine out and tell everyone the truth
strings.把这一个月里发生的事，原原本本告诉他们: Tell them everything that happened this month, exactly as it was
strings.把那桶水抬回来——这种时候，谁的水都是大家的: Carry that drum of water back — at a time like this, anyone's water is everyone's
strings.抗风桐上扑腾了半夜。鸟血是温的，带着腥味，可每个人都喝了。: Wings beat in the trees half the night. The blood is warm and rank, but everyone drinks it.
strings.抢先跑过去，一脚把狗踹开: Run over first and kick the dog away
strings.抬上北头的高地，挖深坑，立一个浮木做的十字: Carry the body up to the high ground at the north end, dig deep, put up a cross of driftwood
strings.抬到阴凉里躺着，多喝水，熬: Lay {actor.him} in the shade, give {actor.him} plenty to drink, and wait it out
strings.拦住他：当着所有人的面，把话说开: Stop him: clear the air, in front of everyone
strings.拼命往回游——离礁盘只有几十米: Swim hard straight back — the reef is only a few dozen metres away
strings.拿到了就是好几天的命；被发现了，对方手里有刀: Get it and you've bought days of life; get caught and they have knives.
strings.拿削尖的木叉和符秀英的鱼钩，到礁盘外缘的深水里叉鱼、钓鱼。收获时多时少，有时一条: With a sharpened wooden spear and Susan Fu's fish hooks, you go into the deep water off the outer edge of the reef flat to spear and line for fish. Some days there is plenty, some days not one; there are currents along the edge, and a big reef fish will poison you now and then.
strings.拿海水冲掉，再用烧红的刀尖烫一烫: Wash them out with seawater, then sear the wound with a red-hot knife point
strings.拿走的水要还回去；换他一个肯留下的理由: The water you took goes back; in exchange, a reason for him to stay
strings.按兰多说的：傍晚在岛中间的洼地挖浅坑，只舀最上面一层: Do what Lando said: at dusk, dig shallow pits in the hollow in the middle of the island and skim only the top layer
strings.按老办法：两边各到岛的一头冷静一夜，明天中午在中间那棵大椰子树下谈: The old way: each side cools off a night at its own end of the island, then at noon tomorrow we talk under the big coconut palm in the middle.
strings.按苏晴说的配“口服补液”：一升开水里放一小撮盐、几勺椰子糖水，病人一口一口不停地: Make oral rehydration the way Chloe says: a pinch of salt and a few spoons of sweet coconut water in a litre of boiled water, given to the sick a sip at a time without stopping
strings.按规矩办：喝多少，扣多少: By the rule: whatever he drank comes off his share
strings.按规矩把两人分开：一个去岛北头，一个去岛南头，冷静一天再说: Separate them by the rules: one to the north end of the island, one to the south, a day to cool off
strings.按规矩：两个人各去岛的一头，明天中午在大椰子树下再说: By the rule: each goes to one end of the island, and they talk at noon tomorrow under the big palm
strings.挖沙井取水: Dig a sand well for water
strings.掏空的椰子树干架在礁岩背阴处，上面盖着椰叶。它能装下一百多升水——足够撑过好几天: The hollowed trunk rests in the shade of the reef rock under a roof of palm fronds. It holds over a hundred litres — enough to ride out several dry days.
strings.推搡了一阵，陆子昂那边的人先松了手。水桶被抬了回来，陆子昂站在石缝前，脸色铁青。: They shoved for a while, then Ryan Lu's people let go first. The drums were carried back. Ryan Lu stood at the crack in the rock, his face livid.
strings.推搡变成了扭打，有人抄起了削尖的木棍。等所有人终于被拉开，沙滩上有血。从那天起，: The shoving turned into a brawl, and someone snatched up a sharpened stick. When they were finally pulled apart there was blood on the sand. From that day on, no one on the island dared sleep alone.
strings.推选一个人驾木筏出海。他要带着几升水和一堆椰子，在外海漂上好几天，靠一角破帆和一: Choose one person to take the raft out to sea. He will carry a few litres of water and a pile of coconuts, drift for days in the open sea, and look for the hand-line boats with a scrap of torn sail and a single oar.
strings.掰一块压缩饼干，把狗引开: Break off a piece of hardtack and lure the dog away
strings.摘一兜回去问问别人: Pick a shirtful and take them back to ask the others
strings.收下他的米，让他自己在南头待着: Take his rice and leave him to himself at the south end.
strings.收拾急救包时，你偷偷把一盒头孢（三天的量）塞进了自己的背包最底下——你怕自己哪天: While packing the first-aid kit you quietly slipped a box of cephalosporin, three days' worth, into the bottom of your own pack — you were afraid that if you were ever hurt, no one would keep the pills for you.
strings.放倒一棵粗椰子树，用刀和火把树干掏空，做成一个能存一百多升水的长槽——1965: Fell a thick coconut palm and hollow the trunk with knife and fire into a long trough that holds over a hundred litres — this is how the Tongan boys stored rainwater in 1965.
strings.放倒椰子树、截成段，用帆船的缆绳和搓出来的椰棕绳捆成木筏，再装上断桅和残帆。砍倒: Fell coconut palms, cut them into lengths, bind them into a raft with the yacht's cable and twisted coconut-fibre rope, and fit the broken mast and the scrap of sail. A felled palm yields a little palm heart to eat, but every tree cut is one coconut less on the island.
strings.救人的人自己也可能被浪拍到珊瑚上: Whoever goes in may be slammed onto the coral by a wave
strings.救她，但不说药是哪来的: She lives, but no one learns where the medicine came from.
strings.救生筏应急包里的纱布、碘伏、缝合针线和止血带。: Gauze, iodine, suture needle and thread, and a tourniquet from the liferaft's emergency kit.
strings.文静、怕给人添麻烦，疼也不吭声。: Quiet, afraid of being a nuisance, and she makes no sound even in pain.
strings.日子照旧。只是从那天起，每个人干活时都会时不时抬头望一眼海面。: The days went on as before. Only from then on, everyone glanced up at the sea now and then while they worked.
strings.日子照旧。干活的人看陆子昂的眼神，一天比一天冷。: The days went on as before. The workers' looks at Ryan Lu grew colder by the day.
strings.早上分水的时候，桶里又少了一截。阿旺的嘴唇是湿的，谁也没有说破。: At the morning water ration the drum was short again. Jay's lips were wet, and no one said a word about it.
strings.早上打水的时候，有人发现储水的水面上浮着一层绿膜，底下有细小的孑孓在游，闻起来一: When they went for water in the morning, someone found a green film floating on the stored water, tiny wrigglers swimming under it and a strange smell. After days of blazing sun the water was turning.
strings.旱了一个礼拜，这天下午，西南边的天一下子黑了。先是一阵凉风，接着是豆大的雨点砸在: After a week of drought, the south-western sky goes black one afternoon. First a cool gust, then fat drops smack onto the scorching rocks and hiss into steam — a thunderstorm is sweeping in from the sea.
strings.旱到第四天，风也停了。水桶见了底，椰子壳里的水要一口一口数着喝。有人舔着裂开的嘴: On the fourth dry day even the wind dies. The barrel is nearly empty and the water in the coconut shells has to be counted out mouthful by mouthful. Someone licks split lips and says: on TV, when explorers run out of water, they drink their own urine.
strings.明天推选人选。走的人凶多吉少，但这可能是最快的出路: Choose the person tomorrow. Whoever goes is more likely lost than saved, but it may be the quickest way out.
strings.晒干的浮木、椰叶和椰子壳。有火的时候每天要烧掉一份。: Sun-dried driftwood, palm fronds and coconut shells. With a fire going, one load burns every day.
strings.晓雨右小腿上留了一道二十多厘米长的疤。回学校以后她退出了帆船社，第二年又重新报了: Ivy was left with a scar more than twenty centimetres long on her right calf. Back at school she quit the sailing club, then signed up again the following year. When someone asked whether she was still afraid, she said: "I am. That's why I have to learn."
strings.晓雨右小腿上那道疤又深又歪，是苏晴一条一条挑完蛆以后缝的。她后来读了昆虫学的研究: The scar on Ivy's right calf is deep and crooked; Chloe stitched it after picking the maggots out one by one. Ivy went on to graduate work in entomology, writing her thesis on tropical blowflies — “I had to find out which kind was in my leg that day.”
strings.晓雨小腿上的口子边缘已经发白，里面还嵌着珊瑚碎屑。苏晴说：珊瑚伤口在热带最容易烂: The edges of the gash on Ivy's calf had gone white, and coral grit was still embedded in it. Chloe Su said: coral wounds rot fastest in the tropics, and it has to be cleaned out and stitched properly — either with the iodine and suture thread from the first-aid kit, or by making do with fishing line and a fish hook ground straight.
strings.晓雨的伤口红肿发烫，渗着黄水，人烧得说胡话，一直喊妈妈。苏晴摸着她滚烫的额头，想: Ivy's wound was red, swollen and hot, weeping yellow, and the fever had her raving, calling for her mother. Chloe Su felt her burning forehead and remembered the box of cephalosporin at the very bottom of her pack, never handed over.
strings.晓雨的帆船社在她的柜子里找到一本没写完的航海日志，最后一页画着一只红脚鲣鸟。从那: Ivy's sailing club found an unfinished logbook in her locker, with a red-footed booby drawn on the last page. Since then, the first lesson of every year's freshman training has been how to treat a coral cut.
strings.晓雨被抬上了黑船的小艇。她一直回头望着，直到铁壳船开出了礁盘。: Ivy was lifted into the black ship's dinghy. She kept looking back until the iron boat cleared the reef.
strings.晓雨被送上岸的时候已经烧到四十度，医生说再晚两天，那条腿就保不住了。她后来转去学: When Ivy was brought ashore her fever had hit forty degrees, and the doctor said that two days more and the leg would have been lost. She later switched to marine biology and wrote her thesis on coral — "I had to know what it was that opened up my leg."
strings.晓雨靠着礁岩坐着，一双手没停过：编集雨的椰叶槽、补渔网、给所有人编帽子。: Ivy sat against the reef rock, her hands never still: weaving palm-frond troughs to catch rain, mending nets, making hats for everyone.
strings.晚上弹给大家听: Play it for everyone in the evening
strings.晚饭时，陆子昂慢条斯理地说：“我算过账。晓雨每天什么都干不了，吃的喝的却跟干活的: At supper Ryan Lu said, unhurried: "I've done the sums. Ivy can't do a thing all day, but she eats and drinks as much as the people who work. I'm not saying we cut her off — I'm saying we have to be efficient." Ivy buried her face in her knees.
strings.普通话很标准，语气温和，爱说“兄弟”“咱们理性一点”“我有个提议”。: Standard Mandarin, a gentle tone; fond of "brother", "let's be rational about this", "I have a proposal".
strings.暴雨灌进了窝棚，一部分存粮和柴火泡了汤。: The storm drove into the shack and soaked part of the food stores and firewood.
strings.暴雨里，窝棚的一角塌了，雨水和沙子一起往里灌，存粮和柴火眼看就要泡汤。推选一个人: In the storm a corner of the shack collapsed, rain and sand pouring in, and the food stores and firewood were about to be ruined. Choose someone to go out in the rain and prop it up again.
strings.最可能把救援带回来的人；也是最不必回来的人: The one most likely to bring back a rescue; and the one with least need to come back.
strings.最快；可要是 payao 早就不在了呢？: Quickest; but what if the payao is long gone?
strings.最快；孩子会看见你踹了它: Fastest; but the boy will see you kick him
strings.最省事，但离窝棚和水太近: The least trouble, but too close to the shack and the water
strings.最管用的办法，可病人每天都要多喝掉不少干净水: The thing that works best; but every patient drinks a lot of extra clean water each day
strings.最能游的人马上下水去拉他: The strongest swimmer goes straight in to pull him out
strings.最费心思，但能让人心不散，夜里的火也有人看着: The most trouble to run, but morale holds and someone is always watching the fire at night
strings.最醒目的办法，要用掉 2 份柴: The most visible option; burns 2 loads of firewood
strings.最难的是先低头: The hardest part is bending first.
strings.最需要救治的人先走: Those who need care most go first
strings.有人发现梁伯这两天走路发飘，嘴唇裂出了血口子。追问之下才知道：每次分水，老人都偷: Someone noticed that Uncle Leo had been unsteady on his feet for the past two days, his lips split and bleeding. Pressed, they learned the truth: every time water was shared out, the old man quietly tipped his own half-shell into Pebble's coconut shell. "I'm sixty-seven. He's twelve." Uncle Leo waved a hand. "At my age, drinking it is a waste."
strings.有人小声嘟囔了一句“扫兴”。可分水的时候，每个人的椰子壳里还是那么浅浅的一层。: Someone mutters “killjoy”. But when the water is shared out, every coconut shell holds the same shallow measure as before.
strings.有人托着他的头，椰子水一口接一口地灌了下去。: Someone holds his head while the coconut water goes in, mouthful after mouthful.
strings.有人把 {protagonist} 按在了沙地上。所有人都转过头，看向赵卫东。: Someone pinned {protagonist} face-down in the sand. Every head turned towards Wesley Zhao.
strings.有人把一根粗木棍塞进赵卫东手里：“规矩立了就得有人执行。你来。”被按在沙地上的人: Someone pressed a thick wooden club into Wesley Zhao's hand. "A rule needs someone to enforce it. You do it." The man pinned in the sand lifted his head and looked at him. Wesley Zhao's knuckles went slowly white around the club.
strings.有人把半桶水推了过去。黑暗里静了很久，然后是脚步声，渐渐远了。: Someone pushed half a drum across. The dark stayed quiet for a long time, then footsteps, fading away.
strings.有人把收走的鱼叉递回到他手里，说了声对不起。兰多掂了掂鱼叉，看了大家很久，把那只: Someone puts the confiscated spear back in his hand and says sorry. Lando weighs it in his palm, looks at them all for a long time, and sets the blue barrel down.
strings.有人把自己的椰子壳往晓雨面前一推：“她吃我的。”没人再说话。: Someone pushed their own coconut shell in front of Ivy: "She eats mine." No one said anything else.
strings.有人朝南头指了指。兰多点点头，像是早就料到了，转身走回了椰林。那天夜里，南头亮起: Someone pointed towards the south end. Lando nodded, as if he had expected it, and walked back to the grove. That night a small fire lit up at the south end.
strings.有人讲起一个帆船圈里流传很广的故事：1965 年，六个汤加孩子在一座荒岛上，就是: Someone told a story that goes round every sailing club: in 1965, six Tongan boys on an uninhabited island lasted fifteen months on these very rules. The group wrote the watch rota out in the sand with sticks.
strings.有人说，五十年代一个法国医生就是这么横渡大西洋的: Someone says a French doctor crossed the Atlantic this way in the fifties
strings.有火能熏干存着，没火大半会臭掉。有人会很难过: With fire we can smoke it and keep it; without, most of it will rot. Someone will be upset.
strings.木棍结结实实地砸在 {actor} 的肩膀上。{actor} 没有还手，也没有让: The stick landed square on {actor}'s shoulder. {actor} didn't hit back and didn't step aside. Jay's arm shook for a long moment; then he threw the stick into the sea and crouched on the sand, crying.
strings.木筏在外海漂到第三天，被一条下钓的渔船发现了。{actor} 指着来时的方向，嗓: On the third day adrift the raft was found by a hand-line fishing boat. {actor} pointed back the way they had come, too hoarse to speak.
strings.木筏在外海被横浪掀翻了。{actor} 抱着两根椰子树干，天黑以后才被潮水推回礁: A cross-sea capsizes the raft out beyond the reef. {actor} clings to two palm trunks and is washed back onto the reef after dark.
strings.木筏在外海被浪打散了。{actor} 抱着两根树干，被潮水推回了礁盘，皮肤晒得起: The raft broke apart in the open sea. {actor} clung to two logs and was carried back to the reef flat by the tide, skin blistered with sunburn.
strings.木筏扎好了。它静静地躺在沙滩上，比所有人想象的都要小。: The raft was finished. It lay quietly on the sand, smaller than anyone had imagined.
strings.木筏扎好了：六根椰子树干，用帆船的缆绳和椰棕绳捆了三道，中间立着一截断桅，挂着一: The raft was finished: six coconut trunks lashed three times over with the yacht's lines and coir rope, a broken mast standing amidships, a scrap of torn sail hanging from it. Whether it could take the open-sea swell, nobody knew.
strings.木筏推下水，划过去拦他们: Push the raft into the water and paddle out to cut them off
strings.木筏留着，什么时候走都行: Keep the raft. It can go any time.
strings.木筏被拖到了高处，用椰叶盖着。每天都有人走过去，摸一摸那几道绳子。: The raft was dragged up high and covered with palm fronds. Every day someone would walk over and touch the lashings.
strings.木筏被推下了礁盘的缺口，一角破帆鼓了起来。: The raft is pushed out through the gap in the reef and its scrap of sail fills.
strings.杀了它——够所有人吃好几天: Kill it — enough meat to feed everyone for days
strings.来接人的船在礁盘外下了锚，上岛的人先闻到了气味，然后看见了南头沙地上那一排浅浅的: The boat anchored outside the reef, and the men who came ashore smelled it first, then saw the row of shallow graves on the sand at the south end. The living were skin and bone, several still running with diarrhoea. The ship's doctor took one look and kept them apart from the crew. Alive to leave: {survivors}. Left on the island: {dead}. What killed them wasn't hunger or the sun but dysentery, passed from one to the next through the camp.
strings.来接他们的船靠上礁盘时，沙滩上点着两堆火：一堆在北头的礁岩下，一堆在南头的椰林里: When the boat came for them, two fires were burning on the sand: one under the reef rock at the north end, one in the palm grove at the south. The two groups boarded the dinghy separately and sat at opposite ends, and the whole way nobody looked at anybody. Those who survived: {survivors}. Those who never made it: {dead}. Afterwards they never gathered once — even at the courthouse they went in by separate doors.
strings.果肉又苦又涩。不到一个小时，{actor} 开始剧烈呕吐，心跳得又乱又慢。后来大: The flesh was bitter and astringent. Inside an hour {actor} was vomiting violently, {actor.his} heartbeat erratic and slow. Only later did they learn it was the sea mango — in the fishing villages of Hainan they call it the suicide fruit, and some who ate it never woke up.
strings.柴火烧光了，火堆在后半夜熄了。: The firewood burned out and the fire died in the small hours.
strings.柴烧光了，煮海水的铝锅停了火。: The firewood has run out; the pots of boiling seawater go cold.
strings.桶、冷藏箱、椰子壳……所有能装水的东西加起来能装多少。下雨时装不下的水只能看着流: The drum, the cooler, the coconut shells... everything that can hold water, added up. Rain you cannot hold simply runs off while you watch.
strings.桶里、冷藏箱里和椰子壳里存着的水。存水不能超过储水容量。: Water stored in the drum, the cooler and coconut shells. Stored water can never exceed your water storage.
strings.梁伯一早上都盯着手表上的气压读数：一天掉了六个百帕。天边是一缕缕马尾一样的卷云，: Uncle Leo spent all morning watching the pressure reading on his watch: six hectopascals lost in a day. On the horizon, streaks of cirrus like horses' tails; the swell running longer with every set; seabirds flying inland since first light. He said it calmly: "Typhoon. Inside two days."
strings.梁伯回到广州，把岛上二十多天的气压读数一笔一笔抄成了一张表，寄给了南海预报中心的: Back in Guangzhou, Uncle Leo copied out his twenty-odd days of island pressure readings, line by line, and posted them to his old colleagues at the South China Sea forecasting centre. There's a stretch of seven days stuck at 1012, and beside it in red he wrote: “Subtropical high. Seven days, no rain. We nearly didn't make it.”

Uncle Leo went back to Guangzhou and copied the island's twenty-odd days of pressure readings into a single table, stroke by stroke, and mailed it to an old colleague at the South China Sea forecasting centre. The table was later pinned up on the forecast-room wall under the title: "The typhoon seen by one wristwatch".
strings.梁伯在沙地上画了海图：“报了位置，船一天半就到了。没到，要么没报，要么报错了——: Uncle Leo draws a chart in the sand. “If he'd reported us, a boat would have come in a day and a half. None came, so either he didn't report it or he got the position wrong — all these reefs look alike. When they search a second time, they have to know at a glance it's us.”
strings.梁伯坚持要守夜：“我这把老骨头，闲着才难受。”随他: Leo insists on keeping watch: “These old bones are worse off idle.” Let him
strings.梁伯埋在了北头的高地上，坟头朝着北边。他的手表被带回广州，交给了他的女儿。她把表: Uncle Leo is buried on the high ground at the north end, his grave facing north. His watch was carried back to Guangzhou and given to his daughter. She set it before her father's portrait, and it kept running.
strings.梁伯埋在了北头的高地上，坟头朝着北边。小石头一直戴着那块手表，每三个钟头看一次，: Uncle Leo is buried on the high ground at the north end, his grave facing north. Pebble wore the watch the whole time, reading it every three hours until the day they boarded the boat. Later he copied the figures scratched into the rock and posted them to the South China Sea forecasting centre — and on the envelope, as sender, wrote “Uncle Leo's apprentice”.
strings.梁伯慢慢把手表又戴了回去，闭上了眼睛。沙地上那行字，第二天就被风吹平了。: Slowly Leo straps the watch back on and closes his eyes. By the next day the wind has smoothed the words in the sand away.
strings.梁伯是把自己的水一口一口省给小石头以后倒下的。他的手表后来戴在了小石头的手腕上，: Uncle Leo collapsed after saving his own water mouthful by mouthful for Pebble. His watch ended up on Pebble's wrist, its dial stopped at the last pressure it had read: 1003 hPa.
strings.梁伯沉默了很久，最后点了点头：“好，我喝。”: Uncle Leo was silent for a long time, then nodded at last: "All right. I'll drink."
strings.梁伯没再坚持，只是把手表摘了下来，挂在窝棚门口最显眼的地方。: Uncle Leo didn't push it. He simply took the watch off and hung it in the most obvious place by the shack door.
strings.梁伯的话说不清了，可脑子是清楚的。他用还能动的左手，把那块带气压计的手表摘了下来: Uncle Leo can no longer speak clearly, but his mind is clear. With his good left hand he takes off the watch with the barometer and writes in the sand, stroke by stroke: “Note the pressure every three hours. Five or six hectopascals down in a day means wind is coming.” He looks at Pebble, then at everyone, and waits.
strings.梁伯躺在高地上，眼睛一直望着北边。: Leo lies on the high ground, his eyes on the north.
strings.梁树生，大家叫他梁伯。在南海预报中心报了三十五年台风，退休后报名参加训练营的离岸: Leo Liang, whom everyone calls Uncle Leo. He forecast typhoons at the South China Sea forecasting centre for thirty-five years; after retiring he signed up for the camp's offshore passage, saying he wanted to "see with his own eyes the sea he had forecast half his life". He wears an outdoor watch with a barometer on his wrist; his blood-pressure pills were soaked in seawater when they abandoned ship.
strings.棍子落下去的声音很闷。赵卫东打了三下就停了手，扔下棍子，一个人走进了黑暗里。那股: The club landed with a dull sound. Wesley Zhao stopped after three blows, dropped the club and walked alone into the dark. There was a ferocity in it that left them all stunned — that was not how ordinary men fought.
strings.椰子一个接一个砸进沙子里，堆成了一座小山。: Coconuts thud into the sand one after another until there's a small mountain of them.
strings.椰子一个接一个砸进沙子里，堆成了一座小山。梁伯坐在小山旁边，一个一个地数。: The coconuts thudded into the sand one after another until they made a small hill. Uncle Leo sat beside it and counted them, one by one.
strings.椰子壳里的补液水有点咸，有点甜。苏晴守在病人中间，一个一个地喂，一个一个地数。: The rehydration water in the coconut shells is a little salty and a little sweet. Chloe sits among the sick, feeding them one by one and counting.
strings.椰子水灌下去，梁伯呛得满脸通红。当天夜里，他开始发烧，呼吸里带着咕噜咕噜的痰音—: The coconut water goes down and Leo chokes, purple in the face. That night he runs a fever and his breathing gurgles — the water went into his lungs.
strings.橙色的救生筏被翻了个底朝天，篷布绑在椰子树上斜拉下来。雨水哗哗地流进筏底，所有人: The orange liferaft was flipped right over, the canopy lashed to a palm and angled down. Rain drummed into the bottom of the raft, and everyone stood in the rain with their mouths open, grinning.
strings.正午的沙滩上一个人影也没有。窝棚底下躺满了人，谁都不说话，连小石头都被按着睡午觉: At midday the beach is empty. The shade is full of people lying still, nobody speaking; even Pebble is made to take a nap.
strings.正午躲进阴凉，只在清早和傍晚干活: Take shelter in the shade at noon; work only at dawn and dusk
strings.正午，一个刺眼的小光点落在干椰棕上，不到一分钟就冒起了烟。: At noon a small, blinding point of light fell on the dry coconut fibre, and in under a minute it was smoking.
strings.正在拉痢疾的人数，决定传得多快。: How many people have dysentery right now; the more there are, the faster it spreads.
strings.母船说，一个礼拜。一个礼拜，又一个礼拜……: Mother boat said one week. One week, and another week...
strings.每个人都得多走几百步、守着规矩；能把病挡在门外: Everyone walks a few hundred paces more and keeps to it; it can keep disease out
strings.每个人都有权决定自己那份水给谁: Everyone has the right to say who gets their own share of water.
strings.每人每天能少出不少汗；干的活少了，找回来的吃的也少: Everyone sweats a good deal less each day; less work also means less food brought in
strings.每天要烧掉两份柴，换四升淡水；柴烧完就停: Two units of firewood a day for four litres of fresh water; it stops when the wood runs out
strings.每晚要多烧大半份柴；夜里的火光比白天的烟传得远: Most of a unit of extra firewood every night; a fire at night carries farther than smoke by day
strings.毒日头连着晒了好几天。正午的礁盘被晒得发烫，沙子能烫起泡；在外面干活的人头晕眼花: The sun blazed down for days on end. At noon the reef flat was too hot to touch and the sand could raise blisters; those working outside went dizzy and bleary-eyed, lips peeling white, shoulders and backs burned red.
strings.比划了半天才弄明白：笼子沉在了暗流口上，鱼进去又被冲出来。兰多是帮她把笼子挪了个: After a lot of gesturing it becomes clear: the trap was sitting in the mouth of a current, and fish were swept out as fast as they went in. Lando had moved it for her and weighted the mouth with a lump of coral.
strings.气压一千零八，稳得很。今天不会下雨，水省着点喝。: Pressure 1008, steady as a rock. No rain today, so go easy on the water.
strings.水不还。要留下，就守这边的规矩: The water stays. If he wants to stay, he follows our rules
strings.水性好的人都会这么想: Any strong swimmer would think so
strings.水桶又满了一截，兑出来的水有一股淡淡的咸味。没人说什么，可每个人喝完都还想再喝。: The barrel is fuller again; the mixed water tastes faintly of salt. Nobody says anything, but everyone wants another drink the moment they finish.
strings.水桶和存粮被分成了两份，分的时候差点打起来。从那天起，两堆火之间的那片沙滩，谁都: The drums and the stores were split in two, and they nearly came to blows over the division. From that day on, nobody would cross the stretch of sand between the two fires.
strings.水用 T 恤滤过一遍，看着清了一些。: The water was strained through a T-shirt and looked a little clearer.
strings.水留给还救得回来的人: Keep the water for those who can still be saved
strings.汪！汪汪！（冲着海面上的一个黑点叫了好一阵）: Woof! Woof woof! (Barks for a long while at a black speck on the water)
strings.沉默、克制、可靠；服从有道理的命令，看不惯欺负弱小；很少表态，一旦表态就不会改。: Silent, restrained, dependable; he obeys an order that makes sense, and cannot stand to see the weak bullied; he rarely takes a position, and once he takes one he never moves. Cornered, his body moves before his mind does.
strings.沉默、警惕、极有耐心。三个月的孤独让他习惯了自言自语，也让他对谁都先留三分；他护: Silent, wary, endlessly patient. Three months alone have left him talking to himself, and holding something back from everyone; he guards his water drum and his nephew's grave like the last of his worldly goods. Once he decides you are his own, he will teach you everything he knows.
strings.沙井里渗出来的地下水是咸的，混进存水里会让人腹泻。下雨能把它冲淡。: The groundwater seeping into the sand well is salty, and mixed into your stores it gives you diarrhoea. Rain dilutes it.
strings.沙滩上摆满了椰子壳、罐头盒、鞋子、塑料袋——任何能盛水的东西。雨停的时候，每一个: The beach was covered with coconut shells, tin cans, shoes, plastic bags — anything that would hold water. When the rain stopped, every one of them was full.
strings.沙滩上用白珊瑚石摆的 SOS、高地上的旗子和烟。暴风雨会把它们冲散。: The SOS laid out in white coral stone on the beach, the flag and the smoke on the high ground. A storm washes them away.
strings.沙滩上的火堆烧得噼啪作响。: The fire on the beach crackled and snapped.
strings.没人会高兴，可水还在桶里: Nobody will thank you, but the water stays in the barrel
strings.没人再说什么，大家各自回去躺下了。只是从那以后，水桶边上总有人睡不踏实。: No one said anything more, and they went back to their places. Only from then on, someone always slept badly beside the water drums.
strings.没人动。陆子昂笑了笑，开始分今天的水：他的人先领，满满一壳；其他人后领。: Nobody moved. Ryan Lu smiled and began handing out the day's water: his people first, a full shell each; the rest after.
strings.没人听得进去。火把被打落在沙地上，扭打又持续了好一阵。: Nobody was listening. The torches were knocked down into the sand and the brawling went on for a long while.
strings.没人知道就没事；被抓到，就是全营地的事: If nobody knows, no harm done; get caught, and it is the whole camp's business.
strings.没有人去碰那只蓝桶。: No one touched the blue drum.
strings.没有人拦他。那天晚上，南头的椰林里亮起了一堆小小的火。: Nobody stops him. That night a small fire glows among the palms at the south end.
strings.没有人说话。大家默默地一个接一个爬上了舢板。: Nobody spoke. One by one they climbed silently into the dinghy.
strings.没有打火机：要靠弓钻钻木取火，大太阳底下借老花镜或望远镜的透镜聚光会快得多。有了: No lighter: fire has to come from a bow drill; in strong sun, focusing light through reading glasses or a binocular lens is much faster. Only with a fire can water be boiled and fish and shellfish cooked (raw food and raw water bring gastroenteritis); the fire eats one unit of firewood a day, and rain, an unwatched night or running out of wood will put it out. Food doesn't keep at thirty degrees: some of it goes off every day, and only smoking over a fire makes it last longer.
strings.没有火，鱼钩只能用船刀刮干净，在海水里泡了又泡。苏晴深吸一口气，开始缝。: There was no fire, so the hook could only be scraped clean with the boat knife and soaked over and over in seawater. Chloe Su took a deep breath and began to stitch.
strings.没等问清楚，就有人饿得先咬了一口。: Before anyone could ask, someone too hungry had already taken a bite.
strings.治伤口感染的唯一办法。: The only cure for an infected wound.
strings.沿着海滩捡浮木、干椰叶和椰子壳，摊在礁岩上晒干。有火的时候每天要烧掉一份；下雨天: Along the beach you pick up driftwood, dry palm fronds and coconut shells and spread them on the reef rock to dry. With a fire going, one load burns every day; anything gathered in the rain comes back wet.
strings.活下来的人后来才知道：坐那条黑船走的陆子昂，上岸第三天就回了家。他没有报警，也没: The survivors only learned the truth later: Ryan Lu, who went on the black ship, was home by his third day ashore. He never told the police or anyone that people were still on the island — he said he remembered nothing of the voyage. The rest held out many more days before a boat came. Those who survived: {survivors}. Those who never made it: {dead}. Asked later about that "ticket", those who came back said only: "He bought it himself."
strings.派一个人驾筏出海，去外礁找下钓的渔船: Send one person out on the raft to find the hand-line boats at the outer reefs
strings.海上听船长的：韩振海说了算: At sea, the captain's word is law: Neil Han decides
strings.海上搜救中心对“海燕号”的搜索投入。船偏离了航线，飞机找的是另一片海；十天后搜索: How much the maritime rescue centre is putting into the search for the Petrel. The yacht strayed off course, so the aircraft are searching the wrong sea; after ten days the search is all but over.
strings.海上的事，看得准，不一定躲得过。: At sea, seeing it coming does not mean you can dodge it.
strings.海南口音的小孩子，说话又快又急。: A small boy with a Hainan accent, talking fast and urgent.
strings.海南口音，管年轻人叫“老弟”“妹仔”，常念叨“海是会吃人的”。: A Hainan accent; she calls young people "little brother" and "girl", and often mutters, "The sea eats people."
strings.海南文昌渔村长大，跟着丈夫在渔船上干了十几年。丈夫出海没再回来以后，她到训练营当: Raised in a fishing village in Wenchang, Hainan, she spent a dozen-odd years working fishing boats with her husband. After he went to sea and did not come back, she took a job as cook and sailor at the training camp. She can mend nets and spear fish, and knows everything on the reef flat that can and cannot be eaten. Her twelve-year-old son Pebble came aboard with her this trip.
strings.海警的船要是来了，你们就说我是你们船上的人，行不行？: If a coastguard boat comes, tell them I am one of your crew, all right?
strings.涨潮了，小石头还在礁盘外缘追一条章鱼。浪已经涌到他的腰，他脚下几步就是陡坎，坎外: The tide was rising and Pebble was still chasing an octopus at the outer edge of the reef flat. The swell was already at his waist; a few steps from his feet the reef dropped away, and beyond the drop the sea was black-blue.
strings.淡水只有四个来源：接雨水（八月是雨季，将近一半的日子有雨；能接多少取决于集雨棚，: Fresh water has only four sources: rain (August is the wet season, and nearly half the days bring rain; how much you catch depends on the rain catcher, how much you keep in containers and the trunk trough), coconuts (about 0.3-0.5 L each; only a few hundred are within reach, only about ten grow a day, and once picked they are gone), groundwater dug from the sand (rain soaks into the coral sand and floats on the seawater as a thin freshwater lens: the nearer the sea and the deeper you dig, the saltier it gets, and salt water gives you diarrhoea and leaves you thirstier; a shallow well in the low ground in the middle of the island, skimming only the top layer, is far fresher; rain dilutes what you have stored), and boiling seawater over a fire to distil it (it costs a lot of firewood and yields a litre or two a day).
strings.清早，东北方很远的海面上出现了一条白色的大船，围着另一片礁盘慢慢地兜圈子，兜了大: Early in the morning a big white ship appears far off to the north-east, circling slowly round another reef. It circles for most of the day — that is the reef they are searching. It's a dozen nautical miles away at least.
strings.清早，梁伯坐在窝棚口，鼻子里的血怎么也止不住，用椰子壳接了小半壳。他说头像要裂开: Early morning: Uncle Leo sits at the mouth of the shack with a nosebleed that won't stop, catching it in half a coconut shell. His head feels as if it will split, he says, and he's seeing double — his blood-pressure pills were soaked in seawater the day they landed, and there isn't one left. It has been hot and dry for days, and he's still keeping the night watch for everyone.
strings.清晨，大家发现水桶、冷藏箱和存粮都被搬到了北头礁岩的石缝里。陆子昂站在石缝前面，: At dawn they found the drums, the cooler and the stores moved into a crack in the reef rock at the north end. Ryan Lu stood in front of it with his people: "From today the water and the food are kept by us and handed out by us. Obey, and you will not lose a mouthful. Refuse — and find your own way."
strings.渔船什么时候来啊？礁岩上的道道我都数不过来了。: When are the fishing boats coming? I can't count the marks on the reef rock any more.
strings.渔船只在外礁下钓——扎好木筏，划过去找他们: The boats only hand-line at the outer reefs — finish the raft and row out to them
strings.渔船来不来是命，先顾好吃喝: Whether a boat comes is fate; food and water come first
strings.渔船经过时更可能被发现，但每天少一个人赶海、捕鱼: More likely to be spotted when a boat passes, but one less person working the reef flat and fishing each day
strings.温和、固执、爱讲道理，老派的知识分子，什么事都要“看数据”。总觉得自己是这群人里: Gentle, stubborn, fond of an argument, an old-school intellectual who wants "the data" for everything. He has always felt he is the least useful of them, and so he keeps trying to give his own share away.
strings.湿椰叶压上火堆，一股浓浓的白烟翻滚着升了起来。: Wet fronds went onto the fire and a thick white column of smoke came rolling up.
strings.潜水机一开，一口气下到二十米，什么都不怕——就怕上来的时候。: Once the compressor starts you go down twenty metres in one breath and fear nothing — only the coming up.
strings.火不能停：拆船板、砍枯树，白天黑夜轮着煮海水: Keep the fire going: break up planks, cut dead trees, and boil seawater day and night in shifts
strings.火光冲天，可那串灯一直没有动，天快亮时消失在了海平线下。: The fire blazed high, but the string of lights never moved, and towards dawn it slipped below the horizon.
strings.火堆边，两个听不懂对方的人说了很久。: By the fire two people who don't share a language talk for a long time.
strings.火把一支接一支地亮了起来。: One torch after another flared up.
strings.火灭了。灰堆里扒了半天，一点火星也没有。生起这堆火有多难，所有人都记得。: The fire was out. They raked through the ashes for a long while: not one spark. Everyone remembered how hard that fire had been to start.
strings.灭了火，躲进灌木丛，等他们走: Douse the fire, hide in the scrub and wait for them to go.
strings.灯光在海面上停住了，然后朝这边移了过来！: The lights stopped on the water — then began moving towards us!
strings.点一支，就说是刚在礁石缝里捡到的: Light one and say you just found it in a rock crevice
strings.点燃高地上的信号火堆: Light the signal fire on the high ground
strings.点起火把，把所有人叫醒：再这样下去，谁也等不到渔船: Light the torches and wake everyone: at this rate none of us will last till a fishing boat comes.
strings.烂肉割了，可没割干净。到了晚上，红肿又往上爬了一截。: The dead flesh is cut away, but not all of it. By evening the redness has crept further up.
strings.烟柱升得很高，可那条船一直没掉头，天黑前消失在了东北边。: The column of smoke climbs high, but the ship never turns; before dark it disappears to the north-east.
strings.热带伤口感染风险是温带的两倍：珊瑚割伤、鱼鳍划伤、晒伤，不及时清创包扎就会化脓发: Wound infection in the tropics runs twice as high as in temperate places: coral cuts, fin scratches and sunburn fester and bring fever if they aren't cleaned and dressed in time; an infection gets worse every day and only antibiotics stop it. Open wounds soaking in reef water can also pick up Vibrio, which can turn a whole leg purple and blistered within a day or two. Stonefish, sea mango and big reef fish (ciguatera) are all poisonous. Dysentery is the commonest killer in a castaway camp: faeces, flies, fingers and food form one chain; someone with diarrhoea needs water and salt, not starving and drinking less.
strings.热带气温：夜里 25–27°C，白天 31–33°C，晴天正午阳光直射的体感再加: Tropical heat: 25-27°C at night, 31-33°C by day, and in direct sun at noon on a clear day add another 10°C to how it feels. Sweat loss per hour is worked out from felt temperature and exertion: even a man in the shade needs 3-4 L a day, and heavy work on the reef flat at noon takes over 7 L; dehydration past 6% of body weight begins to hurt you, past 15% kills.
strings.热水能破坏毒素，前提是有火: Hot water destroys the toxin — if you have fire
strings.照样按份分：船没靠上礁盘之前，什么都不算数: Keep to the shares: until a boat is actually at the reef, nothing counts
strings.照电视里教的，在沙地上挖几个太阳能蒸馏坑，盖上塑料布: Do what they teach on TV: dig solar stills in the sand and cover them with plastic
strings.爬树摘嫩椰子，拿椰子水一口一口喂: Climb for young coconuts and feed {actor.him} the water a sip at a time
strings.狂风卷着暴雨横着打过来，浪头漫上了礁盘，椰子一个接一个往下砸。: The gale drives the rain in sideways, waves wash over the reef flat, and coconuts come down one after another.
strings.用尽量烫的热水泡脚: Soak the foot in the hottest water you can stand
strings.用布滤一滤接着喝，渴死比拉死快: Strain it through cloth and keep drinking — thirst kills faster than diarrhoea
strings.用弓钻在干木板上一圈一圈地钻，钻出火星再吹进干椰棕里。很累，手掌会磨出血泡；大太: With a bow drill you bore into a dry plank, round and round, until a spark comes, then blow it into dry coconut fibre. It is hard work and your palms blister; in strong sun, focusing light with reading glasses or a lens is far quicker. In rain it is all but impossible.
strings.用急救包彻底清创缝合: Clean it out and stitch it properly with the first-aid kit
strings.用掉 1 份急救用品，感染的风险会小很多: Uses 1 first-aid unit; the risk of infection drops a great deal
strings.用椰子树干、缆绳和椰棕绳扎的木筏。暴风雨会把没绑牢的半成品打散。: A raft lashed from coconut trunks, cable and coir rope. A storm breaks up any half-built one that is not tied down tight.
strings.用海水冲一冲，包起来就行: Rinse it with seawater and wrap it up
strings.用鱼线和磨直的鱼钩缝: Stitch it with fishing line and a straightened fish hook
strings.电视里都这么演: That's what they do on TV
strings.留着——万一自己也感染了呢: Keep it — what if you get an infection too
strings.病人们被扶到了南头。夜里，那边传来压低了的哭声。: The sick are helped down to the south end. In the night there is muffled crying from that direction.
strings.病人的椰子壳被收走了一半。苏晴吵了半天，没人听。: Half the patients' coconut shells are taken away. Chloe argues for a long time; nobody listens.
strings.痢疾还要在营地里传多少天。: How many more days the dysentery will keep spreading through the camp.
strings.白得几十升水和一只两百升的大桶；桶的主人恐怕不会善罢甘休: Tens of litres of water for free, and a 200-litre drum; the owner is unlikely to let it go
strings.白珊瑚石摆成的箭头，从棚子门口一直指到椰林外面。那天晚上，守夜的人总觉得南头有人: The arrow of white coral stones ran from the shelter door out past the palm grove. That night the fire watch kept feeling that someone at the south end was watching their fire.
strings.省下一口吃的；这个口子一开，下一个就可能是你: One mouthful saved; once that door opens, you could be next
strings.省下它那一口；它能不能活，看它自己: Saves his mouthful; whether he lives is up to him
strings.省下急救包，效果看苏晴的手艺: Saves the first-aid kit; the result depends on Chloe Su's skill
strings.省事，也看不见了；可岛中间的沙子底下，正是你们挖井取水的那层淡水: Easy, and out of sight; but under the sand in the middle of the island lies the same layer of fresh water your wells draw from
strings.省力，但血腥味会把鲨鱼引到礁盘边上: Less work, but the smell of blood will draw sharks to the edge of the reef
strings.省汗不省水：太阳底下一律不干活，活都挪到清早和傍晚，正午全躲进阴凉，少说话、少动: Ration sweat, not water: no work in the sun — all jobs at dawn and dusk, everyone in the shade at midday, talking and moving as little as possible
strings.看一个人，有时候比听他说话准: Watching a man can tell you more than listening to him
strings.看什么看？我又冇偷你们的。: What are you looking at? I never stole anything of yours.
strings.看有没有人劝得动；劝不动，谁都下不来台: It depends whether anyone can talk him round; if not, nobody can back down
strings.看有没有人镇得住场面: See whether anyone can hold the camp together.
strings.看着半槽水哗哗地流进沙子里，有人别过了脸。: Watching half a trough of water gurgle away into the sand, someone turned their face aside.
strings.看着最干脆；海水里的细菌、烫伤的创面都是新的麻烦: Looks the most decisive; but bacteria in seawater and a burned wound bed are new trouble
strings.看着最着急、最心疼: It looks the most caring and the most urgent
strings.看见那几缕马尾云没有？高空在转风，过两天天要变。: See those wisps of mare's-tail cloud? The wind is turning high up; the weather changes in a day or two.
strings.真有这种疗法；可热带的苍蝇不止一种，有的蛆连活肉也吃: Maggot therapy is real; but there's more than one kind of fly in the tropics, and some larvae eat living flesh too
strings.真相会摆在所有人面前: The truth comes out in front of everyone.
strings.眼下的水有了；树摘空了，后面的日子就靠不上它们了: Water for now; but once the trees are stripped, you can't count on them later
strings.眼不见心不烦，但两边都会过得更难: Out of sight, out of mind — but both sides will have a harder time of it.
strings.砍椰叶、扎木架，把礁岩下的窝棚搭得更大、更结实，顶上铺三层椰叶。窝棚漏雨，人就睡: Cut palm fronds, lash a timber frame, and make the shack under the reef rock bigger and stronger, with three layers of fronds on the roof. A leaking shack means poor sleep and fevers, and no keeping the stores or the fire safe; a storm will tear away a great piece of it.
strings.礁岩上已经刻了十二道划痕。会算日子的人掰着指头一算：今天是八月十六号，南海的伏季: Twelve notches were already cut into the reef rock. Whoever was keeping the count worked it out on his fingers: today was 16 August, and the summer fishing ban in the South China Sea was over. From today, boats from Tanmen and Wenchang would come back to these outer reefs to hand-line and gather sea cucumbers — if they passed, the island had to show them something they could see.
strings.礁岩下的窝棚: The shack under the reef rock
strings.礁盘上的贝类、海参和小鱼，翻得越勤越少，要慢慢长回来。: Shellfish, sea cucumbers and small fish on the reef flat; the harder you work it, the thinner it gets, and it grows back slowly.
strings.礁盘外缘的“海燕号”残骸: The wreck of the Petrel on the outer reef flat
strings.离岸流只有几十米宽: A rip like this is only a few dozen metres wide
strings.私下找他：分我一半，我就当没看见: Go to him privately: give me half and I'll never mention it
strings.稳妥一些，但放一夜的鱼会坏掉一部分: Safer, but a night lying out spoils part of the fish
strings.稳妥一点；他会记住是谁动的手: Safer that way; he'll remember who took it.
strings.稳妥；可兰多已经等了三个月，他不一定听你们的: Safer; but Lando has waited three months already, and he may not listen to you
strings.窝棚底下躺了一排人，谁也不说话，只听见海浪和自己的心跳。: A row of people lies in the shade without a word; all anyone can hear is the surf and their own heartbeat.
strings.立个规矩：守火的人睡着了，扣他一天的口粮: Make a rule: whoever sleeps on the fire watch loses a day's ration
strings.立个规矩；可赵卫东发过誓: It sets an example; but Wesley Zhao swore an oath
strings.立什么规矩，各凭良心: What rules? Everyone goes by their own conscience
strings.立威。这个口子一开，以后就收不住了: It makes an example. Open that door once and there is no closing it
strings.立规矩，也立了仇: It sets a rule, and makes an enemy
strings.站到他那边，以后分东西会有你一份: Stand with him and you'll get a share when things are handed out
strings.站在礁盘边看着——兰多一直把孩子挡在浅水那边: Stand at the reef's edge and watch — Lando keeps the boy on the shallow side all the time
strings.站符秀英：笼子是她的，他得认: Back Susan Fu: it's her trap and he has to own up
strings.站陆子昂：一个酒气熏天开船撞礁的人，凭什么还说了算: Side with Ryan Lu: a man who ran the boat onto a reef while reeking of drink — what right has he to go on giving orders
strings.站韩振海：船长的话就是命令: Side with Neil Han: the captain's word is an order
strings.符秀英一口咬定，她那晚什么也没看见。: Susan Fu insisted, flatly, that she had seen nothing that night.
strings.符秀英一把揪住儿子的耳朵往回拖。小石头一路哭一路喊：“他教我认潮水！他教我的！”: Susan Fu grabs her son by the ear and hauls him back. Pebble cries the whole way: “He was teaching me the tides! He was teaching me!”
strings.符秀英一看就变了脸色，一把把果子全扔进了海里：“海杧果！吃一个就能要人命！”: One look and Susan Fu's face changed; she snatched up the fruit and threw it all into the sea. "Sea mango! One is enough to kill you!"
strings.符秀英下在礁盘上的鱼笼被人提过了——绳结的打法不一样。她拎着空笼子走到兰多面前，: Someone has hauled Susan Fu's fish trap on the reef — the knot is tied differently. She carries the empty trap over to Lando, swears at him in Hainanese, then switches to Mandarin: “My husband's boat went down on a reef to the south three years ago. In his last phone call he said there were foreign boats all round.” Lando doesn't understand a word, but he understands the look in her eyes.
strings.符秀英和小石头都留在了那座岛上。后来潭门的渔民经过那片礁盘，总会往海里撒一把米。: Both Susan Fu and Pebble stayed on that island. Afterwards, when Tanmen fishermen passed the reef flat they always scattered a handful of rice into the sea. They say a woman from Wenchang sleeps there, and that no one mended nets better than she did.
strings.符秀英在事故听证会上作了证，说出了那天后半夜在舵位边看见的事。回到文昌，有人说她: Susan Fu testified at the accident hearing and told what she had seen by the helm in the small hours. Back in Wenchang, some said she was ungrateful, others that she had done right. She offered no defence; she sent Pebble to school in Haikou and opened a small restaurant in Puqian.
strings.符秀英带着小石头回了文昌。第二年开海，一条从巴拉望来的邦卡船在潭门港外靠了岸，船: Susan Fu took Pebble home to Wenchang. When the next fishing season opened, a banca from Palawan put in outside Tanmen harbour, and the man aboard asked for “Big Sister Fu from Wenchang” by name. That night she cooked a whole table of coconut rice, and two old fishermen with no common language gestured their way through an entire bottle of rice wine.
strings.符秀英带着小石头回了文昌，在铺前镇开了一家小饭馆，招牌菜是椰子饭。她再也没让小石: Susan Fu took Pebble back to Wenchang and opened a small restaurant in Puqian, where the signature dish is coconut rice. She never let Pebble on a boat again — but whenever the closed season ends she stands on the dock and watches the boats head out, one after another.
strings.符秀英把儿子的名字、家里的电话写在一块椰子壳上，塞进了他的裤兜。: Susan Fu wrote her son's name and the family's phone number on a piece of coconut shell and pushed it into his trouser pocket.
strings.符秀英搓椰棕绳的速度比兰多还快。兰多看着她的手，竖了一下大拇指。: Susan Fu twists coir rope faster than Lando does. He watches her hands and gives a thumbs-up.
strings.符秀英摘下老花镜，用衣角擦了又擦。: Susan Fu took off her reading glasses and polished them on the hem of her shirt, over and over.
strings.符秀英没能活着离开那座岛。小石头被送回文昌的外婆家，十八岁那年考上了海南的一所海: Susan Fu did not leave that island alive. Pebble was sent back to his grandmother's in Wenchang; at eighteen he was admitted to a maritime college in Hainan to study navigation. In the "ambition" box on the form he wrote: "To be a captain who never lets his ship hit a reef."
strings.符秀英站了很久，最后说：“我男人的事，跟你没关系。是我心里过不去。”兰多听不懂，: Susan Fu stands there a long time, and finally says: “What happened to my husband has nothing to do with you. It's me who can't let it go.” Lando doesn't understand, but he puts the blue barrel down.
strings.符秀英被赶走以后，一个人在南头的礁石间赶海、叉鱼，比谁都熬得住。来接人的船靠岸时: After Susan Fu was driven out she worked the rocks at the south end alone, gleaning and spearing fish, and outlasted them all. When the rescue boat came in she stood on the reef flat and did not say a word.
strings.第一口下去就有人吐了。脱水的人尿得又少又浓，里面全是身体要排出去的盐和废物——喝: The first mouthful makes someone throw up. A dehydrated body makes little urine, thick with the salts and waste it's trying to get rid of — drinking it only makes the thirst worse.
strings.第三天傍晚，木筏的残骸被浪推回了礁盘，上面没有人。: On the evening of the third day the wreckage of the raft was washed back onto the reef flat. There was no one aboard.
strings.第二天一早，阿旺的铺位空了，水桶里少了一截。南头的椰林里升起了一缕烟。: Next morning Jay's bed is empty and the water barrel is lower. A thread of smoke rises from the palms at the south end.
strings.第二天中午，两个人在大椰子树下坐了很久，谁也听不懂谁，可最后谁都没再提那个笼子。: At noon the next day the two of them sit a long time under the big palm, neither understanding the other — but neither mentions the trap again.
strings.第二天中午，两拨人在大椰子树下坐了一个下午。没有人道歉，但傍晚的时候，南头的火被: At noon the next day the two groups sat under the big palm all afternoon. Nobody apologised, but by evening the fire from the south end had been carried back under the reef rock.
strings.第二天傍晚，一条刷着蓝白两色的菲律宾渔船出现在外礁，船头站着兰多。他找到了村里的: The next evening a blue-and-white Filipino boat appeared outside the reef, Lando at the bow. He had found the village's payao and waited for the mother ship that took the catch. The men aboard talked in Tagalog, English and gestures; the islanders understood one word: "Salamat" — thank you. Those who lived to board: {survivors}. Those who never made it: {dead}. A man who had lasted three months alone there finally brought the living home.
strings.第二天傍晚，梁伯能自己咽下一小口水了。: By the next evening Leo can swallow a sip of water on his own.
strings.第二天分水的时候，{protagonist} 的椰子壳里只有浅浅的一层。: When the water was shared out the next day, {protagonist}'s coconut shell held barely a finger's depth.
strings.第二天天亮，邦卡船和兰多都不见了，沙滩上只留下一道拖痕，一直通进海里。: At daybreak the bangka and Lando were both gone; only a drag mark was left on the beach, running down into the sea.
strings.第二天当着所有人的面说出来: Say it in front of everyone the next day
strings.第二天早上，晓雨的烧退了一些。没人知道为什么。: By the next morning Ivy's fever had come down a little. Nobody knew why.
strings.第二天，{actor} 和陆子昂在一起的时间明显多了。: The next day {actor} was plainly spending more time with Ryan Lu.
strings.第二天，{actor} 和陆子昂谁也没提昨晚的事。: The next day neither {actor} nor Ryan Lu mentioned the night before.
strings.第二天，伤口反而更深了——这一窝蛆连活肉也在啃。晓雨疼得整夜说胡话。: The next day the wound is deeper — these maggots are eating living flesh too. Ivy is delirious with pain all night.
strings.第二天，陆子昂黑着脸跟着去了椰林，抱回来一堆椰子，手掌磨破了皮。: The next day Ryan Lu went to the palm grove scowling and came back with an armful of coconuts, his palms skinned raw.
strings.第四天傍晚，所有人围坐在礁岩下。韩振海说：“这个岛上得有规矩。”陆子昂笑了笑：“: On the evening of the fourth day everyone sat round under the reef rock. Neil Han said: "This island needs rules." Ryan Lu smiled: "Rules are fine, but first let us be clear — who makes them, and who enforces them."
strings.等回去了，我要跟全班讲这个岛，他们肯定不信。: When we get back I'm telling the whole class about this island. They won't believe me.
strings.等它下完蛋，挖走一半，放它回海里: Wait for it to finish laying, take half the eggs and let it go back to the sea
strings.答应他：船来了，就说他是我们船上的水手: Promise him: when the boat comes, we'll say he was one of our crew
strings.简单直接。只要他还是领头人，人心就稳；他一旦下台，这条规矩就成了笑话: Simple and direct. While he leads, morale holds; the moment he falls, the rule becomes a joke
strings.米是好米，人就不一定了: The rice is good rice. The man is another matter.
strings.红光在夜空里炸开。几分钟后，远处的灯光开始朝这边移动。: The red light burst in the night sky. Minutes later the distant lights began moving towards us.
strings.红光在大太阳底下显得那么暗。飞机没有转向。: In the blazing sun the red light looked dim. The plane did not turn.
strings.红光炸开几分钟后，远处的灯光开始朝这边移动。: Minutes after the red light burst, the distant lights began moving towards us.
strings.细路，过来，梁伯教你认星星：那颗最亮的是织女星，往北走就是家。: Little one, come here. Uncle Leo will teach you the stars: that brightest one is Vega — head north from there and you are home.
strings.绑了他，让赵卫东教训教训他：坏了信号，就是要大家的命: Tie him up and let Wesley Zhao teach him a lesson: wrecking the signal could kill us all
strings.给他十升水和一兜椰子，让他一个人去: Give him 10 L of water and a bag of coconuts and let him go alone
strings.给他派活：明天跟着去爬椰子树: Give him a job: tomorrow he goes up the palms with the rest
strings.给他留点面子，他会记你的情: You let him keep some face, and he will remember it.
strings.给大家一个交代，又不真下手: Settles it for everyone without really hurting him
strings.给晓雨换药的时候，苏晴的手停住了：纱布底下的伤口里有东西在动——一窝白色的蛆，在: Changing Ivy's dressing, Chloe Su's hands freeze: something is moving in the wound under the gauze — a nest of white maggots, burrowing in the rotten flesh. Ivy takes one look and faints without a sound.
strings.罗兰多·迪松，大家叫他兰多，菲律宾巴拉望岛的渔民。五月里，他和十八岁的侄子跟着一: Rolando Dizon, known to everyone as Lando, a fisherman from Palawan in the Philippines. In May he and his eighteen-year-old nephew went out with a mother boat and were left on this reef flat to fish from a small bangka, told the boat would come back for the catch in a week. It never did. The nephew died of a fever in June and lies buried in the palm grove at the south end. Lando has lived ever since on rainwater caught in a blue plastic drum.
strings.老人很倔，未必听得进去: The old man is stubborn; he may not take it in
strings.老辈人说，拉肚子就得饿着、少喝，喝多少拉多少: The old folks say: starve a flux and drink little — what goes in comes straight out
strings.能吃苦、精明、护犊子；对有钱人天生不信任；表面上听船长的，心里只装着儿子。: Hardy, sharp, fierce about her boy; she distrusts rich people on instinct; to the captain's face she does as she is told, but her heart holds only her son.
strings.能多存很多水，但救生筏就再也下不了海了，扎木筏得从头来: You can store far more water, but the liferaft will never go to sea again, and the raft must be built from scratch
strings.能存多少，看容器和集雨棚: How much you keep depends on your containers and catcher
strings.能少传几个人；病人没人照顾，会觉得被扔下了: Fewer will catch it; but the sick will be left without care and will feel abandoned
strings.能抓多少抓多少，喝血解渴，肉熏干了存着: Take as many as you can, drink the blood to quench your thirst, smoke the meat and store it
strings.能捞回吃的、水桶、帆布和工具，但礁盘上全是锋利的珊瑚: You can bring back food, water drums, canvas and tools, but the reef flat is all sharp coral
strings.能省下吃的和水；可这句老话是错的: It saves food and water; but the old saying is wrong
strings.能装水的东西全拿出来，椰子壳一个个摆满沙滩: Bring out everything that can hold water and line the beach with coconut shells
strings.腿上这口子，一到晚上就一跳一跳地疼。: This gash on my leg throbs all night.
strings.自己也抄起鱼叉走过去：要叉，三个人一起叉: Pick up a spear and wade out too: if there's fishing to do, the three of them do it together
strings.自负、要面子、有担当；习惯发号施令，听不得质疑；心里压着事故的愧疚，所以对所有人: Conceited, touchy about face, and willing to carry the weight; used to giving orders and unable to stand being questioned; guilt over the accident presses on him, so he is especially hard on everyone, and harder still on himself.
strings.舱里全是海水和碎玻璃钢，什么也没捞到: The cabin was nothing but seawater and shattered fibreglass; nothing was salvaged
strings.舵位底下的储物格里卡着一个空朗姆酒瓶: An empty rum bottle jammed in the locker under the helm
strings.船也许只是晚了，再等等: Maybe the boat is just late. Wait
strings.船老大带着两个拎砍刀的人上了岸，打量了你们很久。他要走了从“海燕号”上捞回来的那: The boat boss came ashore with two men carrying machetes and looked you over for a long time. He took the coil of stainless steel cable salvaged from the Petrel and threw down a drum of water and half a bag of rice: "The boat's small, we don't call at proper ports. One person, at most. Give me your answer before daylight."
strings.船老大耸耸肩，把烟头弹进海里，转身走了。: The boat boss shrugged, flicked his cigarette butt into the sea and walked away.
strings.船老大说下个月来接我。他会来的——他还欠我三个月工钱。: The skipper said he would come for me next month. He will come — he still owes me three months' wages.
strings.船老大蹲在沙滩上，听了很久，一根接一根地抽烟。: The skipper crouched on the sand, listened for a long time and smoked one cigarette after another.
strings.船靠近礁盘时，岛上的人已经说不出话来，只会一遍一遍地挥手。活着离开的是：{sur: When the boat came in over the reef flat, the people on the island had no words left; they could only wave, over and over. Those who left alive: {survivors}. Those who stayed on the island: {dead}. The accident report on the Petrel ran to many pages; of what happened on the island in those days, it said not a word.
strings.船靠近礁盘的时候，来接他们的人愣住了：沙滩上有两堆熄灭的篝火，隔着一片椰林遥遥相: When the boat closed on the reef, those who came for them froze: two dead cookfires on the sand, facing each other across the palm grove. Those who came forward were gaunt, sharp sticks in their fists, keeping apart. Those who lived to board: {survivors}. Still on the island: {dead}. Asked later about that month, none would go into detail. Someone remembered the novel: boys cast away, spearing their own until an officer reached the beach.
strings.苍蝇一天比一天多，饭一端出来就落满一层。有人在离集雨的地方不到二十步的灌木后面踩: There are more flies every day; the moment food is set out it's covered. Someone treads in a pile of faeces behind the bushes not twenty paces from where the rain is collected — the island is small and everyone goes wherever is nearest. Anchor has just run back from there and is nosing at the water barrel again. Chloe Su says: “That's how dysentery travels: faeces, flies, fingers, mouths.”
